stem: A 6-year-old has parotid-region swelling; which additional oral structures should be checked on examination?

options.text: Uvula, tonsils, and posterior pharyngeal wall
Tongue, floor of mouth, and lower lip
Maxillary frenum, central incisors, and palate
Buccal sulcus, upper lip, and nasal septum

explanation: Uvula, tonsils, and posterior pharyngeal wall are the additional structures to inspect in a child with parotid-region swelling. This completes the oral examination beyond looking at the parotid duct area.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because these are the additional structures specifically checked as part of the oral examination in parotid-region swelling.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because these structures are not the specific additional areas named for this examination.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because these are not the listed structures to check in parotid-region swelling.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the frenum and incisors are not the targeted additional examination areas here.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because this combination does not match the structures specified for the assessment.
